text.p: Following are the main stories from Austrian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Foreign Minister and Wolfgang Schuessel's position as conservative People's Party leader is under debate by regional party heads.
- Milk prices are being raised by up to 0.6 schillings by some supermarket chains.

- The introduction of pension reforms is stalling due to continuing negotiations between the government and civil servants. Economy chamber president Leopold Maderthaner is now boycotting the discussions.
- Leading manufacturer of water treatment technology BWT reported a six percent drop in pre-tax profit due to a significantly lower financial result in the first half of 1996.
- The future of Leykam remains open although a decision on choice of partner should be made this week.
- Quality badges will replace stars as quality criteria for hotels.
- Austrian Airlines has an ambitious savings plan, aiming to reduce costs by 12 percent and launch a successful sales offensive.

- Police investigations into the so-called Bajuwarische Befreiungs Armee which claims responsibility for a spate of racially motivated letterbombs are progressing steadily. Police are on the trail of five suspects.
- Some hundreds of asylum seekers are pursuing criminal goals, according to Interior Minister Karl Schloegl, who plans a new criminal crackdown.
- Mobilkom and max.mobil both plan to lodge a complaint to the EU Commission in Brussels over the award of Austria's third mobile phone licence to the Connect Austria consortium.
- Economy Minister Hannes Farnleitner to test oil price regulation on the basis of agreement. BP head Guido Fortis wants more freedom for petrol station shops and the right to sell tobacco wares.
- Investigations of letterbombers look like they could flop, although Interior Minister Schloegl remains optimistic.
- Sponsors remain loyal to the festival. Since 1990 businesses have poured millions of schillings into the Salzburg festival.
- The partial privatisation of the postal savings bank P.S.K. will not happen until next year.
